why: AHABI is a named, validated self-report assessment instrument rather than a general instructional element.
name: AHABI (Self-rated skills for research-based learning) questionnaire
product_description: A 20-item Likert-scale self-administered questionnaire developed by Cobos Alvarado et al. to measure undergraduate students' self-rated research skills for research-based learning.

why: The AHRQ knowledge transfer framework is an implementation and evidence-to-practice framework, not a general theory of how people learn or are taught.
AHaH is a named Java-based astronomy teaching software product rather than a general instructional element.
name: AHaH — Appreciating Hubble at Hyper-speed Java visualization tool
product_description: A Java-based interactive three-dimensional visualization tool developed by Liam J. Nolan et al. for teaching redshift, galaxy morphology, Hubble's Law, and cosmological parameters in introductory astronomy.

why: This describes two astronomy lab implementations for first-year students using the AHaH tool, rather than a general reusable instructional pattern.
